newsitem.title: MEXICO: Alestra sets single rate for Mexican phone calls.
newsitem.headline: Alestra sets single rate for Mexican phone calls.

text.p: Alestra, one of the new long-distance telephone carriers competing in the recently liberalised Mexican market, has announced a single-rate plan of 1.30 pesos per minute for calls anywhere in Mexico at any time.
Alestra, a joint venture of AT&T, Mexican industrial group Alfa and Mexican bank Bancomer said in a news relase that its single rate was the lowest on offer in Mexico.
Like other competitors, Alestra also offers a plan that includes two separate rates, one for weekdays and another for nights and weekends.
Alestra claimed that all of its rates were lower than those of the main competition, Telmex, and Avantel, a joint venture by Mexican bank Banamex and MCI Corp.
